evidence.finding: Candidate c133a5a3 target case: Task Duration 42.98 us, Block Dim 512 (per-block rows 512). Per-block means: aiv_time 3.18 us, mte2_time 1.51 us (ratio 0.473), mte3_time 0.663 us (ratio 0.217), vec_time 0.668 us (ratio 0.217), scalar_time 0.784 us (ratio 0.240). mte3_wait_ratio 0.654, vec_wait_ratio 0.464. 512/40 cores = 12.8 serial programs per core, so kernel duration ~= 12.8 x per-program time: the kernel is a serial chain of small per-program load->vector->store tiles, not a bandwidth wall (mte2 active bw 33 GB/s/core; read hit rate 75%).

core0.veccore0 partial 6.6 us window (absolute_time_qualified=false, application_completed=false): MTE2 productive 0.701 / idle 0.299; MTE3 productive 0.153 / wait_only 0.704 / idle 0.143; VECTOR productive 0.101 / wait_only 0.649 / idle 0.250; SCALAR productive 0.069. Store engine and vector engine sit in explicit WAIT most of the observed window while MTE2 is productive: consistent with a producer->consumer dependency chain per tile. Idle intervals are observed window gaps, not proven stalls, and the window is partial, so this only distinguishes hypotheses.

The target-case IR is straight-line: three 128x64 tt.load (q,k,v), three 64-wide bias loads, then q extf/addf/mulf/truncf and three 128x64 tt.store. No loop and no independent second tile exist in a program, so within a program there is nothing the compiler can overlap with the tile's own MTE2 stream: the dependency chain load->compute->store is structurally serial.

attempt-002 (a5afde4c) -> attempt-003 (c133a5a3) doubled the per-program tile (8 KB -> 16 KB element budget) and cut target latency 0.07936 -> 0.06351 ms, so amortizing per-program cost over more bytes is a demonstrated mechanism. attempt-004/005 (bb15ccd3, 28d7c8a2) failed compilation with 'ub overflow, requires 2146304 bits while 1572864 bits available', i.e. ~262 KB requested against a 192 KB UB: growing the live tile set is the blocking constraint. attempt-001 (deca261a) is a numeric fp16-overflow failure and stays a constraint to keep the fp32 opmath ordering.

The rejected grouped-head attempt used 3-D tiles tensor<32x4x16x!tt.ptr<f16>> (and tensor<32x1x1> out offsets). The 3-D grouped layout is what the lowering could not fit into UB, so any new work-grouping must stay 2-D [BLOCK_S, BLOCK_D] with [BLOCK_S] row offsets.

Retained best c133a5a3 passes 21/21 formal cases, geo_mean 1.6235, target-case speedup 1.435 (63.51 us vs 91.14 us reference), min speedup 1.361. This is the baseline any new candidate must not regress.

hypothesis: For the exact (unmasked) path the per-program body is a single dependent chain: load q/k/v -> vector compute -> store q/k/v, and the compiler has no second tile to overlap, so per core the chain repeats serially 12.8 times. If one program processes GROUP=2 consecutive seq blocks in a 2-D loop marked tl.range(..., num_stages=2), the Ascend multi-buffering can issue tile i+1's MTE2 while tile i is still in vector/store, overlapping the 1.51 us MTE2 with the ~0.66 us MTE3 and ~0.67 us vector work; bias loads and pid decomposition are also amortized once per 2 tiles. Live UB stays 3x(16 KB in + 16 KB out) plus one extra load stage, well inside the 192 KB budget that blocked larger single tiles.
alternatives: Grow BLOCK_S to 256 with the current six-live-tile structure: rejected, 6 x 32 KB = 192 KB already exceeds the UB budget (attempt-004/005 overflow lesson), and it is the same transformation class that already failed.

Widen BLOCK_D to 256 (4 heads) so input rows become 512 B contiguous DMA segments: rejected for now because output addressing becomes piecewise per head; the earlier 3-D grouped layout [S,4,16] is exactly what overflowed UB, and a piecewise 2-D store risks scatter lowering.

Only reduce program count (in-program loop with no pipelining): expected <=3% because Amdahl on the 0.4-0.6 us per-program fixed cost is small and 256 blocks / 40 cores has ~9% wave quantization; kept as the fallback prediction if num_stages does not pipeline.
discriminating_observation: After the change, per-block mean aiv_time over the 256 blocks should be below 2 x 3.18 = 6.36 us (overlap achieved) and the per-block vec_wait_ratio / mte3_wait_ratio should drop from 0.464 / 0.654; if aiv_time is ~2 x 3.18 us with unchanged wait ratios, the loop did not pipeline and the mechanism is rejected. Paired Task Duration (42.98 us baseline) and formal target-case latency (63.51 us baseline) are the outcome measures.
change: EXACT path only: give each program GROUP consecutive seq blocks via a tl.range(0, GROUP, num_stages=2) loop with 2-D [BLOCK_S, BLOCK_D] tiles; hoist the three bias loads and the pid decomposition outside the loop; grid becomes batch*num_heads*num_seq_groups. GROUP=2 only when block_d==head_dim, seq_len % block_s == 0 and num_seq_blocks % 2 == 0; otherwise GROUP=1 and the existing masked/unmasked behaviour is preserved unchanged (mask now uses the loop row index). Wrapper math, strides, dtype/opmath order (fp32 q add+mul then one cast; fp16 k/v add) and output allocation are unchanged.
expected: Paired candidate Task Duration 42.98 -> ~36-39 us (10-15%) if the next tile's MTE2 overlaps the current tile's vector+MTE3; formal target-case latency 63.51 -> <=60 us with identical numerics; per-block mte2_time roughly doubles while aiv_time grows less than 2x.
validation: decision --record; then preflight --source candidate.py (compile + 48 supplementary cases); on awaiting_source_review hand off unchanged; host runs the 21-case formal evaluation, comparing target-case latency and all other cases against c133a5a3.
layer_reason: The evidence localises the loss to per-tile serialization (MTE3 wait_only 0.70, VECTOR wait_only 0.65, per-program aiv_time 3.18 us with only 0.67 us productive vector), and the IR shows a straight-line body with no independent work to overlap. Only a kernel-structure change can put a second independent tile in flight; host-side allocation or launch changes cannot.
simulator_incremental_judgment: Hotspots add: the largest instruction-time entries are the kernel-entry BAR (5.65 us, line 35), a WAIT_FLAG before the q store (4.65 us, line 113) and three VECTOR BARs around the q add/scale/cast (4.38-4.62 us, lines 107-109), i.e. the synchronisation points sit exactly on the load->vector->store chain; they locate the dependency points but their sums overlap other pipelines and cannot be added to a duration, so they do not by themselves separate pipelining from bandwidth. Waiting/observable idle adds: MTE3 wait_only 0.70 and VECTOR wait_only 0.65 versus MTE2 productive 0.70 distinguish a producer/consumer serialization from a load-bandwidth limit; the 0.25 VECTOR and 0.14 MTE3 idle fractions are observed partial-window gaps only, not proven causal stalls. Simulator-incremental: neither report was needed to prove a full-device time; both were used only to choose the overlap hypothesis.

post_edit_state.note: Preflight returned awaiting_source_review before any device action; candidate.py is handed off unchanged and unmeasured. No device, simulator or formal observation exists yet for this source SHA, so the discriminating observation above must be read against newly collected evidence for 4bfa839d, not against c133a5a3.

unknown: Whether the Ascend Triton lowering honours tl.range(..., num_stages=2) with multi-buffering; if not, the loop degenerates to the no-pipelining fallback.
Whether 2-stage buffering of 3 x 16 KB in-tiles plus 3 x 16 KB out-tiles fits the 192 KB UB without the multi-buffer overflow seen in attempt-004/005.
Wave quantisation: 256 blocks on 40 cores is 6.4 blocks/core, so ~9% tail loss may offset part of the overlap gain.
